answer: A wide orchard of purported identities does not erase the delay: each identity must complete a chain of sequential modular squarings, with every result feeding the next. GPUs may run separate clone chains concurrently, but cannot parallelize the steps within one chain to shorten its elapsed time. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check the work efficiently; sustaining more identities still demands more computation. The horizon is bounded by physical time, not a quill-written claim.
